gaps.title: One note per meeting conflicts with any member writing and only the author editing
gaps.description: DEC-001 says any team member can write notes for any of the team's meetings, and DEC-002 says a meeting has one note. REQ-003 says only the author can edit a note unless edit access is shared. Together these leave it unresolved what a second team member can do when a meeting's single note already has an author: whether they can contribute at all, and who becomes the author of a meeting's note.
gaps.why_it_matters: The note screen (SCR-002) shows a single Notes box per meeting, so whoever writes first would decide whether other team members can contribute to the team's record of that meeting.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Team members who are promised they can write notes for any meeting may be locked out of a meeting's only note, or the author-only edit rule is silently broken.

gaps.title: Visibility of a note before it is shared
gaps.description: The decisions say the author shares a note with named team members as viewer or editor, but not who can see a note that has not been shared: only the author, or every team member. It is also not stated whether team members can see that a meeting already has a note they cannot open.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'Who can open a meeting's notes?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The Meeting notes list (SCR-001) offers an Open link on every meeting row; whether that link works for a team member depends on the default visibility, which neither the requirements nor the decisions set.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Private meeting notes could be exposed to the whole team, or shared team notes could be hidden from people expected to read them.

gaps.title: Sharing flow not shown in the capture
gaps.description: The Share button on the note screen has no captured destination. The confirmed sharing behaviour (choose named team members, set viewer or editor, viewer by default, change or withdraw access later) has no screen, component or flow in the inventory, and there is no observed place where the author can see who currently has access.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing and edit-access grants are two of the three confirmed requirements, and the only entry point observed is a Share button that leads nowhere in the capture.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The access-granting, role-changing and revocation steps cannot be specified, so REQ-002 and REQ-003 cannot be delivered as agreed.
research_questions: What are established interaction patterns for sharing a document with named people at viewer or editor level and later changing or removing that access (for example Google Docs or Microsoft 365 share dialogs)?
How do comparable tools show the current access list of a document to its owner?

gaps.title: Viewer and no-access states of the note screen not shown
gaps.description: Only the default, editable-looking state of the note screen was captured. What a viewer, an editor, the project lead or a team member without access sees on SCR-002 (read-only notes, availability of Save and Share) is not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Viewer is the default access level, so most people opening a shared note would see a state that the mockup does not show.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Viewers may be offered Save or Share controls they are not allowed to use, or permission enforcement is left undefined in the UI.
research_questions: How do collaborative note or document tools present read-only access to viewers and indicate the user's access level?

gaps.title: Concurrent editing by author and editors
gaps.description: Once the author grants editor access, more than one person can change the meeting's single note. Behaviour when two people edit at the same time, and whether anyone sees that their view is stale, is not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-005 'What happens on concurrent edits?'

gaps.why_it_matters: A meeting has exactly one note, so all editors write into the same record; the explicit Save button suggests whole-note saves that can overwrite each other.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Edits made by one editor can be silently lost when another saves.
research_questions: What conflict-handling approaches (locking, last-write-wins with warning, merge, real-time co-editing) are common for shared plain notes, and what are their trade-offs?

gaps.title: Save behaviour, feedback and unsaved changes
gaps.description: The Save button has no captured result. Whether edits are only kept on Save or also autosaved, what confirms success or reports failure, and what happens to unsaved text when the user leaves the screen or the connection drops are not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-004 'Are edits autosaved or only saved via Save?'
ambiguous_behaviours SCR-005 'What feedback is shown on success or failure?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Writing notes is the core action of REQ-001, often done live during a meeting, so lost text is the most likely user-facing failure.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes typed during a meeting can be lost without the writer knowing.
research_questions: What are common patterns for explicit save versus autosave with draft recovery in web note editors?
How should save success and failure be announced to meet WCAG 2.2 success criterion 4.1.3 Status Messages?

gaps.title: Access withdrawn or changed while someone is working
gaps.description: The author can change or withdraw access at any time. What an editor sees if their access is downgraded or removed while they have unsaved edits open, and what happens to those edits, is not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-003 verbatim 'the author can change or withdraw access at any time'

gaps.why_it_matters: Access changes are explicitly allowed at any time, so a mid-edit change is an expected case, not an edge case.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may save changes after losing permission, or lose work without explanation.
research_questions: How do shared-document tools handle a collaborator's access being revoked or downgraded while they have the document open?

gaps.title: Note deletion not shown and its consequences undefined
gaps.description: DEC-005 says only the author can delete a note, but no delete control is shown in the capture. Whether deletion asks for confirmation, can be undone, what happens to existing shares, and whether the meeting can then get a new note are not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: DEC-005 verbatim 'Only the author can delete a note.'

gaps.why_it_matters: A meeting has one note that editors and viewers may rely on; one action by the author removes it for everyone it was shared with.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Shared team notes can be lost irreversibly, and the delete behaviour cannot be specified.
research_questions: What confirmation and recovery (undo window, trash) patterns are common for deleting shared documents?

gaps.title: Rights after the author leaves the team
gaps.description: DEC-005 says the project lead can edit a note whose author has left. It is not stated whether the project lead can also share, change or withdraw access, or delete; what happens to access the departed author granted; whether access is removed for viewers and editors who themselves leave the team; and how a project lead is identified.
gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing and deletion are author-only, so once the author leaves nobody may be able to manage access or remove the note; team membership is also what defines who may be shared with.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes become unmanageable after an author departs, and people who leave the team may keep access to team notes.

gaps.title: Dependence on the team's shared calendar
gaps.description: Meetings come from the team's shared calendar. What happens to a meeting's note when the calendar event is renamed, rescheduled or deleted, how recurring meetings map to notes, where the attendee count comes from, and what users see when the calendar is unavailable are not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-002 'Where does the attendee count come from and can it change?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The meetings list and the note's title, date and attendee count all come from an external calendar, so calendar changes and outages directly affect which notes users can reach.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes can become orphaned or attached to the wrong meeting, and the list can fail with no defined behaviour.
research_questions: Which calendar platform holds the team's shared calendar, and how does its API report event updates, cancellations and recurring-event instances (for example Google Calendar API or Microsoft Graph events and change notifications)?
What rate limits and failure modes apply to reading shared calendar events from that platform?

gaps.title: Meeting list empty, loading, error and volume behaviour
gaps.description: Only one meeting row in a default state was captured. Empty, loading and error states of the meetings list are not shown in the capture, nor are sorting, paging, filtering, or how far back and forward in the calendar the list reaches.
gaps.checklist_item: Empty, loading, success and error states

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-003 'Is the list paged, sorted or filtered, and what does it show when empty?'

gaps.why_it_matters: A team calendar accumulates many meetings over time, and this list is the only observed way to reach a meeting's note.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Users may not be able to find older meetings' notes, and new teams see an unexplained empty table.
research_questions: What default ordering, date-range and paging patterns do meeting-notes tools use for calendar-derived meeting lists?

gaps.title: Note content format and limits
gaps.description: Whether a note is plain text, rich text or can include attachments, and whether there are length limits or other validation, is not defined. The Notes box shows no required marker and no limits in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-004 'Are there length or format validation rules?'

gaps.why_it_matters: The note is the only content this feature stores; its format determines what writers can record and what viewers see.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes may be truncated or rejected unexpectedly, or the editor delivered does not match what the team expects to write.

gaps.title: Notification when a note is shared or access changes
gaps.description: It is not defined whether team members are told when a note is shared with them or when their access is changed or withdrawn, or by which channel.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-006 'What does sharing do (link, email, permissions)?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Sharing is to named team members; without some indication they may never learn a note was shared with them.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Shared notes go unread, or users are surprised when access disappears.

gaps.title: No observed way back from the note screen
gaps.description: The note screen shows only Save and Share; no link back to the Meeting notes list is shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: Writers move between meetings in the list; leaving the note screen interacts with the undefined unsaved-changes behaviour.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Navigation between notes is unspecified and users may leave with unsaved edits.

gaps.title: Record of access changes
gaps.description: Whether sharing, access changes, withdrawals, edits by editors or the project lead, and deletions must be traceable (who, what, when) is not defined.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-005 'Can a save be undone or earlier versions restored?'

gaps.why_it_matters: Several people (author, editors, project lead) can change a single note and its access, so disputes about who changed what are plausible.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Unwanted changes or access grants cannot be traced or reverted.

assumptions.text: The answers recorded in DEC-001 to DEC-005 are treated as the customer's answers to CQ-001 to CQ-005, although each was matched to its question by keywords.
assumptions.why: The decisions' interpretation field says the matching was keyword-based.
assumptions.impact: Questions treated as answered were not raised as gaps.
assumptions.to_confirm: That each verbatim answer was meant for the question it is attached to.

assumptions.text: Each project team has exactly one identifiable project lead.
assumptions.why: DEC-005 refers to 'the team's project lead' without defining the role.
assumptions.impact: Author-departure handling depends on this role existing.
assumptions.to_confirm: Whether every team has a project lead and how that role is recorded.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Any team member may write notes for any meeting (DEC-001), but a meeting has one note (DEC-002) that only its author can edit (REQ-003). See GAP-001.
Author-only editing of a meeting's single note contradicts any team member writing notes for any meeting (DEC-001, DEC-002). See GAP-001.
Visibility of a note that has not been shared is not stated. See GAP-002.
